log: The item in progress kept the price its previous owner was quoted, so a city captured from the computer charged the player the computer's difficulty multiplier. A new Captured rule, civ1-city:city/captured/reprice-build, calls CityBuild.reprice() (core-city-build 0.1.16) (civ-clone/web-renderer#500).

Replaces civ1-city:city/captured/reprice-build with civ1-city:city/captured/clear-build, which calls CityBuild.cancel() (core-city-build 0.1.17) after stop-auto, so BuildingCancelled doesn't choose for the city. The new owner is asked like any city with nothing in production. Civ1 keeps the item; this deliberately doesn't (civ-clone/web-renderer#670, #500).

The test registered only a Warrior and no BuildPriority, so autoBuild could never choose anything and the test passed with clear-build before stop-auto. It now offers an improvement Auto would pick, and fails if the order is swapped.

A BuildCostModifier can depend on who owns the city (civ1-difficulty's computer multiplier does), but CityBuild priced the item once, in build(), through a BuildItem that caches its cost. reprice() replaces the BuildItem for the same item and city and resets the cost from it, keeping progress. A ruleset calls it when the city changes hands (civ-clone/web-renderer#500).

Clears the item and its cost, keeps the progress, and processes the BuildingCancelled rules, as revalidate() did inline; revalidate() now calls it. A ruleset uses it to clear a captured city's build (civ-clone/web-renderer#670).
